title: Progressive-economy routing: personal notes and sketch PRD
content:
Notes to self — quick brain dump for an Economy Routing feature (progressive-fidelity approach).

Context / Why: users want low-cost fallbacks and predictable unit economics on bursty workloads. We already have cost-ladder fallbacks, but rule sets are brittle and tie to hard model tiers. Idea: make a small, heuristic-first routing layer that picks lower-cost model paths based on inferred user intent, session budget, and live signals (latency pressure, KV cache hit, tenant policy).

Goal (MVP):
- Reduce per-token cost for eligible traffic by ~25% on targeted flows while keeping relevant quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-eval proxies) within 5% of baseline.
- Provide a per-tenant opt-in config and a user-session override.
- Surface clear telemetry: routed fraction, failover count, quality regressions by prompt bucket.

Non-goals:
- Not an LLM re-ranker or response transformer yet. No novel model training.
- Not replacing Dedicated routing policies or enterprise explicit pinning (those override our heuristics).

Key concepts / sketch:
1) Intent classifier (lightweight): quick signal (<=25ms) that buckets request into: transient/utility vs exploratory/opinionated vs creative. Use small fine-tuned classifier where possible (or rules by route).
2) Session budget: remaining token budget for session (configurable per tenant). If low, prefer compact responses.
3) Fidelity ladder: a set of compatible model variants (e.g., redwood-1-large -> redwood-1-medium-quant -> redwood-mini-quant). Each rung has metadata: cost factor, expected latency, degradation risk (tagged by test-suite failures).
4) Live constraints: if tail latency > SLO or GPU pressure high, prefer lower rung. Conversely, if KV cache hits strongly predict short completions, we can keep higher rung cheaply.
5) Safe fallbacks: deterministic fallback matrix (if lower rung breaks output contract e.g., hallucination rate > threshold then escalate).

User stories (MVP):
- As a product owner, I can enable Economy Mode for a tenant and set: budget_per_session_tokens, allowed_model_rungs, and intent-sensitivity.
- As a developer, I can mark routes as ineligible (e.g., payments/billing endpoints).
- As an SRE, I can view the routed traffic heatmap and see per-rung error rates and rollbacks.
- As a user, the session can request ‘prefetch-high-fidelity’ to override for a single reply (consumes token budget).

Acceptance criteria (rough):
- Config UI + API to set per-tenant budget and allowed rungs (console + API).
- Routing decision algorithm emits a deterministic decision event for each request (model_rung, reason_code, score).
- Telemetry: percent routed to economy, cost delta vs baseline, per-prompt-set quality delta.
- Canary rollout tool: ability to enable for X% of traffic, with automatic rollback if quality regressions exceed threshold for 30m.

Example routing decision pseudo-flow:
- Input: route="search-snippet", session_budget=150 tokens, user_intent=utility, latency_slo_ok=true, kv_cache_hit=0.9
- Decision: keep on medium rung because cache hit predicts short tokens and intent=utility -> chosen=medium-quant, reason=[intent:utility, cache:high]

Metrics to track (prioritized):
- routed_fraction_by_route (hourly)
- mean_cost_per_request_by_route
- quality_delta_by_prompt_set (A/B) — automated micro-evals on sample traffic
- failover_rate (% of economy->high-fidelity due to quality signal)
- session_budget_exhaustion_rate

Telemetry / eval design notes:
- Need a lightweight synthetic evaluation harness that replays a sampled set of recent requests through both baseline and economy ladder and compares outputs with embeddeding-sim or label-derived signals. Schedule nightly micro-evals per tenant.
- Tag prompts into small buckets: system, short-fact, code, creative. Different tolerances per bucket.

Operational constraints / safety:
- Enterprise pinning always wins. Any route with compliance label (PII, payments) must be excluded.
- Keep deterministic logging for every decision for audit. Include model checksums.
- Rollback policy: if micro-eval quality delta > 5% for >30m and failover_rate < 1% (i.e., fallbacks not catching failures) => auto disable for tenant.

API surface (rough):
- PATCH /tenants/{id}/economy-config {enabled, budget_per_session_tokens, allowed_rungs:[list], intent_sensitivity:int(0-100)}
- GET /telemetry/tenants/{id}/economy-summary?window=1h
- Decision event schema (small): request_id, tenant, route, chosen_rung, decision_reasons[], cost_estimate

Rollout plan (experiment-first):
1) Internal opt-in for product team on low-risk routes (short answers, snippet generation) — 5% traffic. Monitor micro-evals and cost.
2) Expand to targeted customers via support opt-in. Gather tenant-level quality deltas.
3) Public console option with toggle + default off for new tenants.

Open questions / things to prototype quickly:
- classifier latency/cost tradeoff: build small transformer vs heuristics by route. Which gives better precision for intent?
- how to represent "expected degradation risk" per rung programmatically? Use nightly micro-eval baseline vs rank of failures?
- session budget UX: should we expose remaining tokens in SDK? Or only server-side enforcement? (SDK makes it explicit to app devs but increases surface area)
- can we piggyback router decisions on existing admission control/queue? Avoid extra RPC hop.

Next steps (for me / immediate):
- sketch a small toy decision function and run it inside local inference playground on sampled logs (RDW-2384).
- write a short experiment plan for the micro-eval harness: sample size, buckets, statistical test. (talk to Mika for micro-eval infra)
- add a console mockup for per-tenant budget + per-route exclusions (quick Figma frames).

Back-of-envelope numbers (toy):
- If 20% of traffic are short-utility responses and we route them down one rung with cost factor 0.6 -> net cost reduction ~8-10% platform-wide. Focus on high-volume low-risk routes first.

Random ideas to keep in pocket:
- allow end-user preference headers (X-Redwood-Fidelity: low/med/high) for mobile apps to explicitly request cheaper replies when on cellular.
- use cached completions fingerprinting: if we have >N cached completions for a prompt prefix, safely use lower rung.

Notes: keep this lightweight and observable — core risk is silent quality regressions. If we can keep a small, developer-facing feedback loop (console + per-route micro-evals) we can iterate quickly.

TODOs:
- [ ] prototype decision function and record decision events in local replay.
- [ ] draft PRD section for console + API.
- [ ] create sample micro-eval suites (short-fact, snippet, creative) with baseline labels.
- [ ] sync with SRE about telemetry retention and rollbacks.

Slack anchors / refs: product-econ thread, RDW-2384 ticket, micro-eval infra (mika).

End of jot. Will refine into a short PRD once prototype numbers exist.
